objective: Activate authenticated, account-isolated app-wide BUKLOD Emergency SOS overlays for nearby eligible recipients and initiating senders across existing screens; preserve SOS R1 anti-abuse and privacy baseline, support response/resolve, minimized chip, missed-push reconciliation and closed-app notification tap routing.
productionBaselineEvidence: Inspected docs/COMMUNITY_HELP_SOS_R1_LOCK.md R1 protected invariants and current default main 3512c1be015d0ad9f70ea07990739b0a4d438147. Existing SOS backend emits authenticated community_emergency notification rows for opted-in fresh presence in density-selected 1/3/5 km radius, current native NotificationProvider routes tapped SOS to generic Public Wall. Actual latest production OTA bundle and device delivery are not verified; this change is DEV until verified RC and production OTA. Reconciled against main 50cf765bad171348547e41cf0800a3b29a3c3da3. Concurrent desktop/web changes have no overlapping SOS paths.
chosenApproach: Keep existing privileged SOS request RPC, 2s hold/local device authentication, Edge fanout, RLS, 1/3/5km recipient eligibility and push webhook unchanged. Add typed in-app event coordination, native push received bridge, root in-app Modal above all routes with sender/recipient state, explicit action buttons and minimized persistent chip. On recipient lookup, verify current-user canonical notification row AND active proximity-gated buklod_help_list_nearby RPC before revealing any incident detail or accepting response. On sender lookup, verify creator-owned emergency via RLS and keep owner resolve available even with stale presence. Avoid per-user Realtime channels; Expo push primary with 45-second bounded foreground inbox fallback and 15-second refresh for one active incident. Web uses authenticated foreground inbox polling. Do not force an OS screen above other apps, claim government Cell Broadcast, or send duplicate push.
selectionRationale: User requests interruptive notification above any BUKLOD page, even when viewing other content, and a sender response console. Existing SOS has server security but no global overlay or targeted app destination. A root host with canonical verification is compatible with current Expo OTA runtime/native modules, respects user opt-in/location privacy, does not rewrite backend/notification systems and avoids 1M-user permanent database subscriptions.
alternativeApproaches: Install an Android full-screen intent/service to open over other apps (rejected: platform restrictions, native rebuild required, not available to ordinary safety apps)
Use Realtime postgres_changes subscription for every signed-in BUKLOD member (rejected: database connection/cost scaling, historic notification subscription removal)
Replace existing HELP/SOS RPCs and push dispatch with a new broadcast service (rejected: threatens locked anti-abuse, authenticated proximity, privacy and idempotence)
Trust data in push notification for incident coordinates or response (rejected: stale tokens/account crossover and spoofable payload)
preserveBehaviors: Emergency SOS continues through protected authenticated send with long press and local authentication, independent of points or ads
1/3/5 km proximity, 5km maximum fan-out, fresh opt-in presence, bounded radius, cooldown, one active emergency, expiry and canonical RLS unchanged
Exact location remains server-side; only approximate distance from nearby RPC shown
Push dispatch stays canonical community_emergency notifications and single webhook, not double Expo push
Android notification channel capabilities and existing runtime remain unchanged; old clients still use fallback channel
Existing message/cluster invite/PTT push routing, background call behavior, other app stacks and drafts unchanged
Recipient actions are server-side authorized by buklod_help_respond; only creator can resolve; no unverified or stale push can reveal incident details
No new per-account Realtime subscription; no extra native dependencies, service permission, backend migrations or schema changes
All accounts own separate dismissed IDs and overlay state; logout clears state; offline never fabricates alert activity or delivery counts
No claim of guaranteed push receipt, OS-level full-screen intrusion, location background service, or emergency-services integration
acceptanceChecks: Sender sees an in-app SOS control overlay after canonical emergency created, even if push fan-out is delayed/fails; can resolve through protected RPC
When an authenticated opted-in recipient receives push while using BUKLOD, an interruptive verified overlay appears above Home, Wall, Cluster, Connect, Profile
App background/closed receives high priority existing notification; tap opens current incident without destroying composer drafts
During reopened session, missed nearby push is discovered via current account's canonical notifications and active proximity RPC
Recipient sees approximate distance, category and message without raw coordinates; can help, on my way, cannot help, flag with confirmation
User can minimize/back; persistent mini indicator remains while incident active; same incident does not repeatedly pop after dismiss
Sender sees real response counts if authorized nearby RPC available; no fabricated physical push receipt metrics
Expired, resolved, unauthorized, no-longer-nearby or wrong-account events fail closed with safe retry, not stale incident detail
No existing SOS baseline invariants weakened, native app identity/runtimes unchanged
Engineering, TypeScript/Performance and Integration/Web checks pass exact PR head before DEV merge; production requires separate verified Android OTA and on-device acceptance
